name: Oinam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Sarangthem, Bobita (2021) An Introduction to the Sound System of Onaeme (listed in Glottolog; not found online)

sources.citation: Patgiri, Bipasha, Amalesh Gope & Bobita Sarangthem (eds.). 2021. The Phonetics and Phonology of Biate, Hrangkhol, Khelma, Onaeme, Purum, Liangmai and Yimchunger. Tezpur: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. Online file = 12 pp front matter only (title, contents, Post's foreword, editors' Introduction pp. viii-x)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Editors' Introduction (p. ix) summarises second-hand: 'Bobita Sarangthem, in her paper An Introduction to the Sound System of Onaeme, examines the Onaeme sound system by introducing segmental phonemes and the presence of two tones in this unclassified language that also reflects the similarities and dissimilarities within the cognate Naga groups.' Contents list the chapter at pp. 68-87; the chapter itself is not in the online file.

sources.citation: Singh, Huiningshumbam Surchandra (comp.) & Madhumita Barbora (ed.). n.d. [c. 2021]. A Onaeme-English-Hindi Trilingual Dictionary. Tezpur: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. 55 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. No introduction or pronunciation guide; headwords carry plain IPA transcriptions (e.g. adokung [adokuŋ], achichang [acicɯŋ]) with no tone or stress marks; only hits for 'tone'/'pitch' are the glosses 'pitcher' and the verb form 'tonalo'.

sources.citation: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. Language page 'Onaeme la (The Language of Onaeme)' and 'Metadata for recordings: Onaemela' (Sarangthem and team, Oinam Hill Village, 21-02-2020; 61 pp)
sources.note: Nothing. Metadata only: alternate name Ngimaila; CFEL code 005_Ona/M_CFEL_TU_2016; villages Oinam hill, Ngamju, Tingsong, Sorboung, Oinam Laila, Taphou Onaeme; status Threatened; list of audio/video recordings (folktales, songs) archived at CFEL.

sources.citation: Dutta, Niharika & Bobita Sarangthem. 2017. Onaeme Leih Dangdo Laireiboung: A Learner's Book of the Onaeme Language (ed. Gautam K. Borah). Tezpur: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. ISBN 978-81-935387-7-7. 96 pp. [Glottolog ref 570832, listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch]
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 1 'The Sound System' (book pp. 4-10 = pp. 18-24) gives 20 consonants and 10 vowels ('The last four of these vowels are dipthongs') with pictured example words in Roman orthography plus IPA; no mention of tone, stress, accent, pitch or syllable structure. Introduction (pp. 1-3) says Onaeme is 'considered unclassified' but 'closely related to the Poumai Naga group'; ~4000 speakers; fieldwork Feb-Mar and Aug 2017. Rest of book is word lists, sentences, folktales, songs.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Oinam [oina1234] and its two reference records (570832 Dutta & Sarangthem 2017; 589915 Veikho 2021)
sources.note: Nothing. Confirms only two references exist for the languoid: the 2017 learner's book (grammar sketch) and Veikho's 2021 Poumai grammar (coded to pmx, cited for the classification comment that Oinam is 'a native language unintelligible to Poumai'). Endangerment: moribund (AES 8a).

sources.citation: Pao, H. Dune Antonia. 2017. A descriptive grammar of Paoula. PhD thesis, Manipur University. Ch. 1.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on Oinam phonology; states that in 'Villages like Oinam, Thiwa, Khongdei and Ngari, the dialect differs so much that they are not mutually intelligible to the majority of the Poumai Naga community speakers.'

sources.citation: Veikho, Sahiinii Lemaina & Barika Khyriem. 2015. Poula phonetics and phonology: An initial overview. In North East Indian Linguistics 7, 47-62. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Nothing about Oinam stress; names 'Ngimaila (spoken in Oinam village)' as one of the Poula varieties showing 'significant phonological and lexical variation' (p. 47). Poula itself: four tones, no stress statement (see poum1235 record).

sources.citation: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. n.d. An Ethnolinguistics Study of Biate, Hrangkhol, Khelma, Onaeme, Purum, Liangmai and Yimkhiung. Tezpur: CFEL. 49 pp. (Onaeme chapter pp. 32-36)
sources.note: Nothing on language structure; ethnography (name 'Onaeme' = 'people smelling like mud', Ngamju village founding, pottery, agriculture); says the language 'is considered unclassified' but 'closely related to the Southern Naga group'.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Oinam (20 pp, by the CFEL linguist who led the 2017-2020 fieldwork); editors' summary says it covers segmental phonemes and two tones, so it is the one place a stress/accent statement or an explicit 'tonal, no stress' remark would appear.

sources.note: Glottolog's only other reference for oina1234; a full Poula grammar whose dialect survey names Oinam/Ngimaila as unintelligible to Poumai; may contain comparative remarks on Oinam prosody and would fix the Poumai-vs-Oinam identity question, but it is not an Oinam description.
